ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left side of the figure is marked with power supply voltage U=10V, with the upper end as the positive sign and the lower end as the negative sign; on the right side there are two 10Ω resistors in series. The upper node is labeled A, the lower node is labeled B, and the middle connection point of the two resistors is grounded, serving as the 0V reference point. Reasoning: The two 10Ω resistors are in series and have equal resistance values, so the total voltage of 10V is evenly distributed across the two resistors, and the voltage across each resistor is 5V. The upper end of the power supply is positive and the lower end is negative, so point A is 5V higher relative to the middle grounding point, and point B is 5V lower relative to the middle grounding point. Therefore, the potential of point A is +5V, and the potential of point B is -5V.

method.method_draft: First describe the circuit: a 10 V source is applied across two equal 10Ω resistors in series; point A is at the top of the upper resistor, point B is at the bottom of the lower resistor, and the junction of the two resistors is grounded. Since the resistors are equal, the 10 V total voltage is divided equally, giving 5 V across each resistor. Taking the grounded midpoint as 0 V, A is 5 V above ground and B is 5 V below ground, so the potentials are (+5 V, -5 V).
